mainTopic: A knife found notched after שחיטה (רב הונא vs. רב חסדא and the rulings that follow), and the Torah source for חזקה from a house with צרעת
overview: The background: a knife was found notched only after the שחיטה. רב הונא forbids the animal, because the notch may have come from the hide during the cut. רב חסדא permits it, because we can blame the notch on a bone hit after the cut. The גמרא explains why רב חסדא is lenient here but strict about a doubt of שהייה or דרסה: here the flaw is in the knife, not in the animal. It gives the final הלכה, which depends on whether a bone was broken, and explains רב חסדא through the neck bone (עצם דמפרקת). It then tests two real rulings against these views: רב יוסף forbidding thirteen animals, and רב כהנא requiring a knife check between every animal. It also explains why those in-between checks do not need a חכם. Next the גמרא asks for the Torah source of חזקה, keeping something in its known status. רבי יונתן brings the כהן who closes up a house with צרעת from its doorway. רב אחא בר יעקב challenges the proof, אביי defends it, and רבא knocks down אביי's answers. A ברייתא is then brought against רב אחא בר יעקב, and the amud ends just as the גמרא begins his reply, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two doubts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא is lenient about the notched knife but strict when there is a doubt about שהייה or דרסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. If both cases involve a doubt, why does רב חסדא forbid the animal in one and permit it in the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case there was a doubt whether the שוחט paused (שהייה) or pressed the knife down (דרסה), and the animal is פסולה. Here there is a doubt whether the knife was notched during the שחיטה or after it, and רב חסדא says it is kosher. The גמרא wants to know what makes these two doubts different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (asks why two cases that look alike are treated differently)
Pausing in the middle of the שחיטה, which makes it invalid
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth, which makes the שחיטה invalid

phrases.english: And what is the difference?
phrases.notes: He's comparing the doubt about pausing or pressing with our doubt about when the knife got notched.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous daf, where רב חסדא's leniency on the notched knife was set next to a doubt about שהייה or דרסה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What logical difference separates a doubt of שהייה or דרסה (forbidden) from a doubt about when the knife was notched (permitted)?

steps.title: The flaw was in the animal versus a flaw in the knife
steps.stepSummary: In the case of שהייה or דרסה, the possible problem is in the animal itself. In the notched-knife case, the problem is in the knife, and nothing is known to be wrong with the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, a flaw developed in the animal. Here, the knife became flawed, but the animal did not become flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. In the earlier case the doubt is about the animal itself. In the knife case, the only known problem is with the knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there is a doubt about שהייה or דרסה, the doubt is about the way the animal was cut, so its status is shaky. With the notched knife, the animal's שחיטה looked fine; we only know the knife is damaged now. So רב חסדא can blame the damage on something that happened after the שחיטה and leave the animal kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A flaw or weakness that raises a doubt

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general idea: a doubt that starts in the animal itself is treated more strictly than a doubt that starts in an outside tool.

phrases.english: There, a flaw developed in the animal itself,
here, the knife became flawed,
but the animal did not become flawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the case of שהייה or דרסה, the doubt is about the animal itself. With the notched knife, only the knife is known to be flawed, so the animal keeps its kosher status.

steps.title: The final הלכה depends on whether a bone was broken
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב הונא (forbidden) when no bone was broken with the knife, and follows רב חסדא (kosher) when a bone was broken with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רב הונא when he did not break a bone with the knife. The הלכה follows רב חסדא when he did break a bone with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling. It splits the cases based on whether the knife was used to break a bone after the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a bone was broken with the knife after the שחיטה, there is an obvious later cause for the notch, so the animal is kosher, as רב חסדא says. If no bone was broken, we fear the knife was notched on the hide during the שחיטה, so the animal is forbidden, as רב הונא says.

keyTerms.meaning: He broke a bone with it (with the knife)

steps.whatToRemember: Practical rule: if no bone was broken, the animal is forbidden (רב הונא). If a bone was broken, it is kosher (רב חסדא).

phrases.english: And the halakha follows Rav Huna,
when he did not break a bone with it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the knife. He means breaking bones with it after the שחיטה was finished.

phrases.english: And the halakha follows Rav Ḥisda,
when he broke a bone with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the logic to giving the practical ruling between רב הונא and רב חסדא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If no bone was broken, the animal is forbidden (רב הונא). If a bone was broken with the knife after the שחיטה, it is kosher (רב חסדא).

steps.title: If no bone was broken, what did the knife hit?
steps.stepSummary: The ruling suggests that רב חסדא himself permits even when no bone was broken. The גמרא asks: then what could have notched the knife, other than the hide during the שחיטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that רב חסדא permits even when no bone was broken? But then on what did the knife get notched?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the ruling describes רב חסדא. If no bone was broken, it is hard to see what רב חסדא could blame the notch on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'follow רב חסדא when a bone was broken' implies that רב חסדא himself permits even without a broken bone. But with no bone in the picture, the only thing left is the hide, which is רב הונא's worry. So how can רב חסדא permit in that case?

phrases.english: This implies that Rav Ḥisda holds it is valid

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שִׁיבֵּר בָּהּ עֶצֶם?
phrases.english: even though he did not break a bone with it?
But then on what did it become notched?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַב חִסְדָּא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שִׁיבֵּר בָּהּ עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the ruling in step 3 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of step 3 that רב חסדא permits even when no bone was broken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With no bone broken, nothing seems left to blame except the hide during the שחיטה, so רב חסדא's leniency seems to have no basis.

steps.title: Blame the neck bone
steps.stepSummary: Even with no other bone broken, the knife may have been notched on the animal's neck bone after the cut was finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that it was notched on the neck bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב חסדא blames the notch on the animal's own neck bone, hit at the end of the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the windpipe and food pipe are cut, the knife can easily strike the neck bone. That gives a cause for the notch that comes after a valid שחיטה, even if no separate bone was broken. So רב חסדא permits even then, while the final הלכה follows him only when a bone was actually broken.

keyTerms.meaning: The neck bone (the bone of the neck joint)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of bone. 'Breaking a bone' in the הלכה means extra bones cut with the knife afterward. The neck bone here is part of the slaughtered animal's own neck, which the knife hits right after the cut.

phrases.english: Say: it became notched on the neck bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies another possible cause of the notch
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a broken bone, the only possible cause is the hide during the שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The neck bone, struck after the שחיטה was finished, is a possible cause, so רב חסדא can permit.

steps.title: רב יוסף forbids thirteen animals
steps.stepSummary: A real case: רב יוסף declared as many as thirteen animals טרפות when a knife was found notched.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident, and רב יוסף declared as many as thirteen animals טרפות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that happened. It is setting up the next question: which view did רב יוסף follow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several animals were slaughtered one after another with the same knife, and the knife was found notched at the end. רב יוסף forbade thirteen of them. The גמרא will now try to match his ruling to רב הונא or רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real case that happened

phrases.english: There was an incident,

phrases.aramaic: וְטָרַף רַב יוֹסֵף עַד תְּלֵיסַר חֵיוָתָא,
phrases.english: and Rav Yosef declared as many as thirteen animals tereifot,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא וְטָרַף רַב יוֹסֵף עַד תְּלֵיסַר חֵיוָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real ruling to test against the argument between רב הונא and רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף forbade as many as thirteen animals slaughtered with a knife later found notched.

steps.title: Did רב יוסף follow רב הונא, forbidding even the first animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רב יוסף followed. Was it רב הונא, so that even the first animal was forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view did he follow? רב הונא's, so that even the first animal was forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion stands behind רב יוסף's ruling. It suggests רב הונא, which would mean every animal, even the first one, was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, the notch may have come from the hide of any animal, including the first. If so, every animal slaughtered with the knife is forbidden.

phrases.english: In line with whom? With Rav Huna,
and even the first one was forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which view lies behind the incident in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רב יוסף follow רב הונא and forbid every animal, including the first?

steps.title: Perhaps רב חסדא, with the first animal permitted
steps.stepSummary: No, it could follow רב חסדא. We blame the notch on the first animal's neck bone, so the first animal is kosher and all the ones after it are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it follows רב חסדא, and the first animal is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling could also fit רב חסדא. In that case only the animals after the first were forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא blames the notch on a neck bone after a שחיטה. If it happened on the first animal's neck bone, that animal's שחיטה was fine. But every later animal was slaughtered with an already notched knife, so they are forbidden.

phrases.english: No, with Rav Ḥisda,
and not counting the first one.
phrases.notes: The notch is blamed on the first animal's neck bone, so only the animals after it are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 7 by showing the ruling can fit רב חסדא too.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling fits רב חסדא if the notch is blamed on the first animal's neck bone. The first animal is kosher and the later ones are forbidden.

steps.title: Second answer: it must be רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: רב יוסף really followed רב הונא. Under רב חסדא's approach, there is no reason to blame the first animal's neck bone rather than the last one's, which would make all the animals kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really it follows רב הונא. If it followed רב חסדא, then since we are already blaming the notch on a neck bone, how do we know it was the first animal's neck bone? Maybe it was the last animal's neck bone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer. רב יוסף's ruling must follow רב הונא, because רב חסדא's approach would not forbid these animals at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's whole approach is to blame the notch on a neck bone in order to be lenient. If we do that, the last animal's neck bone is just as good a choice as the first one's. Then every שחיטה was done with a good knife and all the animals are kosher. Since רב יוסף forbade them, he must have followed רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second answer
Really, actually: returns to the first idea
We attribute or hang the doubt on a cause

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers about רב יוסף. One: he followed רב חסדא and permitted only the first animal. Two: he followed רב הונא, because רב חסדא's logic would permit every animal.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: really it follows Rav Huna,
for if it followed Rav Ḥisda,
since we are already attributing the notch to a cause,
how do we know it was notched on the neck bone of the first one?
Perhaps it was notched on the neck bone of the last one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that brings back the suggestion of step 7 and argues against the answer in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second answer (איבעית אימא) showing why the other view does not fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף could have followed רב חסדא, blaming the first animal's neck bone and forbidding the rest.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רב חסדא, the notch could just as well be blamed on the last animal, which would permit them all. So רב יוסף's ruling must follow רב הונא.

steps.title: רב כהנא requires checking the knife between every animal
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא tells רב אשי that רב כהנא required the knife to be checked between each animal slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: רב כהנא requires a check of the knife between each and every animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports another practical ruling: according to רב כהנא, a שוחט slaughtering many animals must check his knife after each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the case of רב יוסף and the thirteen animals. If the knife is checked between animals, a notch cannot cast doubt on a long line of animals. The question that follows is which approach this ruling fits.

keyTerms.meaning: A check or examination (here, of the knife)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
Rav Kahana requires an examination
phrases.notes: He means checking the knife for notches.

phrases.english: between each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second practical ruling about a notched knife, after רב יוסף's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The knife must be checked between every single slaughter.

steps.title: Does רב כהנא follow רב הונא, to forbid the earlier animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רב כהנא followed. Maybe רב הונא's, and the check is needed so that only the animal just slaughtered becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רב הונא's, and the check is so that only the first one is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion רב כהנא's rule is built on, and suggests רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, a notched knife forbids the animal slaughtered with it, since we cannot assume the notch came after the cut. Checking after each animal means a notch only forbids the one animal just slaughtered, and not a whole row of them.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
Like Rav Huna, and the check is to disqualify the first one?
phrases.notes: So if a notch shows up, only the animal just slaughtered is lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion step 10's ruling is based on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב כהנא's ruling based on רב הונא's view, so that a notch forbids the animal just slaughtered?

steps.title: It can follow רב חסדא, to make the later animals kosher
steps.stepSummary: No, it can follow רב חסדא. The check is needed so that the later animals stay kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it follows רב חסדא, and the check is so that the later ones are kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב כהנא's rule can also fit רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב חסדא, a notch found afterward can be blamed on the neck bone of the animal just slaughtered, so that animal is kosher. The check between animals protects the next animals: if the knife was clean before each one, each later animal is clearly kosher.

phrases.english: No, like Rav Chisda,
and the check is to make the later ones kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns down the need to say רב הונא, the same way step 8 did for רב יוסף.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling fits רב חסדא as well: the check makes sure the animals after it are kosher.

steps.title: Then each check should need a חכם
steps.stepSummary: If the knife is checked before each animal, every check should need a חכם, like the first check before slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should also need a check by a חכם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: if every slaughter needs a fresh check, why doesn't each check need a חכם like the first one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל required the knife to be shown to a חכם before slaughtering. If each animal now needs its own check, the same requirement should seemingly apply to every one of these checks.

keyTerms.meaning: A check done by a Torah scholar

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, תִּיבְעֵי נָמֵי בְּדִיקַת חָכָם!
phrases.english: If so, it should also require the examination of a sage!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, תִּיבְעֵי נָמֵי בְּדִיקַת חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the check required in step 10 is carried out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The checks between each animal that רב כהנא requires.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first knife check needs a חכם, so every later check should need one too.

steps.title: One witness is believed in איסורין
steps.stepSummary: The שוחט himself can check, because one witness is believed in matters of איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness is believed in matters of איסורין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שוחט himself is believed when he says the knife is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In questions of permitted and forbidden, one trustworthy person is enough. So the שוחט can check the knife alone, and no חכם is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness is believed in matters of what is forbidden or permitted

phrases.english: One witness is believed in matters of prohibition.
phrases.notes: The one witness here is the שוחט himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a general rule of believability
steps.terutzMaskana: The שוחט is believed alone, because one witness is enough for איסורין.

steps.title: Then even the first check should not need a חכם
steps.stepSummary: If one witness is believed, why does the first check before slaughtering need a חכם at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even at the start a חכם should not be needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: if the שוחט is believed, the first check should not need a חכם either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 14 seems to prove too much. If one witness is enough, the original rule of showing the knife to a חכם seems to have no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, at the beginning

phrases.english: If so, at the start also it should not be needed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the first check needs a חכם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one witness is believed, the first check should not need a חכם either.

steps.title: Showing the knife to a חכם is only for his honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said the knife is shown to a חכם only out of respect for him, so one time at the start is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יוחנן say: they only said to show the knife to a חכם because of the חכם's honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the first check is shown to a חכם for respect, not because the שוחט cannot be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about believability; it is about honoring the חכם. Once that honor was given at the start, the later checks between animals can be done by the שוחט alone.

keyTerms.meaning: To show the knife to a Torah scholar
The honor of the Torah scholar

steps.whatToRemember: The שוחט is believed to check his own knife. Showing it to a חכם at the start is only a matter of honor, so the checks between animals do not need a חכם.

phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
They only said to show the knife to a sage
because of the honor of the sage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and closes this discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכם is needed because the שוחט is not trusted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכם is shown the knife only for honor, so it is needed only once.

steps.title: Where do we learn to keep something in its known status?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: what is the source for the rule of חזקה, keeping a matter in its known status?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this thing that the רבנן said: keep the matter in its known status?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule that we assume things stay as they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion so far has relied on assuming things stay as they were, like treating a living animal as forbidden until it is properly slaughtered. Now the גמרא asks where in the Torah this way of thinking comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Keep the matter in its known status (the rule of חזקה)
The status something is known to have, which we assume continues
Where is this matter learned from?

phrases.english: From where is this thing that the Rabbis said:
Establish a matter on its presumptive status?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the source for the rule of חזקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the rule of keeping something in its known status.

steps.title: The פסוק about closing up a house with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן brings the פסוק that the כהן leaves the house, stands at its doorway, and closes it up for seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: the פסוק says, "The כהן shall go out of the house to the doorway of the house, and close up the house for seven days."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source: a פסוק about a house with צרעת. The proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן sees the mark inside the house, but he only declares the house closed after he walks out to the doorway. That time gap is what the proof will be built on.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall close it up (put it in quarantine)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said,
the verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְיָצָא הַכֹּהֵן מִן הַבַּיִת אֶל פֶּתַח הַבָּיִת
phrases.english: "And the priest shall go out of the house to the doorway of the house,
and close up the house for seven days."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק about the כהן closing up a house with צרעת from its doorway.

steps.title: The mark might have shrunk, so we must rely on חזקה
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the mark shrank while the כהן was walking out. The only reason he can still close the house is that we keep things in their known status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe while he was going out, the mark got smaller than the needed size! Rather, isn't it because we say: keep it in its known status?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The כהן can close up the house without seeing the mark again, which shows that the Torah relies on חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between seeing the mark and reaching the door, the mark could have shrunk below the size for צרעת. The Torah still tells him to close the house. That works only if we assume the mark stayed as it was when he last saw it.

keyTerms.meaning: It became less than the required size
Rather, is it not that... (introduces the conclusion of a proof)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of חזקה comes from the house with צרעת: the כהן closes it from the doorway, assuming the mark he saw is still there.
steps.confusionAlert: The question "maybe the mark shrank" is not an attack on רבי יונתן. It is part of his proof: it shows why the פסוק only makes sense if we rely on חזקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a main source for the rule of חזקה, used all over ש"ס whenever we are unsure if something has changed.

phrases.english: Perhaps while he was going out and coming
phrases.notes: He means walking from the mark inside the house out to the doorway.

phrases.english: it became less than the required size!
Rather, is it not because we say:
establish it on its presumptive status.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אַדְּנָפֵיק וְאָתֵא בְּצַר לֵיהּ שִׁיעוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 18 proves the rule of חזקה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule of אוקי מילתא אחזקיה (keeping something in its known status).
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 14:38: the כהן closes the house from the doorway, without seeing the mark again.

steps.title: Maybe the כהן walked out backward
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב suggests the כהן walked out backward and watched the mark the whole time, so the פסוק proves nothing about חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objects: Maybe the כהן went out backward, so he could see the mark while he was leaving!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks the proof from Step 19. He offers a way to read the פסוק where the כהן never loses sight of the mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the כהן not seeing the mark while he walked to the doorway. If he walked out backward with his eyes on it, he would know its size the whole time. Then there is no need to rely on חזקה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (raises a strong challenge)
Backward, walking with his back first

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov objects to it:
phrases.notes: "It" means the proof from the house with צרעת in Step 19.

phrases.english: And perhaps it is a case where he went out backward,
so that he sees it as he goes out!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in Step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for חזקה from the house with צרעת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כהן might have kept watching the mark, so there was never any doubt about it.

steps.title: אביי gives two answers to save the proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that walking backward does not count as 'going out,' and anyway a mark behind the door could not be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: There are two answers. First, going out backward is not called going out. Second, if the mark is behind the door, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי יונתן's proof against רב אחא בר יעקב with two separate answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: the פסוק says the כהן 'goes out,' and walking backward does not count as going out. Answer two: even walking backward, a mark on the wall behind the door would be hidden from him. In that case he must still rely on חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two answers to this matter

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
There are two answers to this matter,
One, that going out backward
is not called going out,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, אֲחוֹרֵי הַדֶּלֶת מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: And furthermore, behind the door, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: He means a mark on the wall behind the door, which the כהן can't see from the doorway even if he walks backward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two independent defenses: the meaning of the word, and a case where seeing is impossible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן could have watched the mark while walking out backward.
steps.terutzMaskana: Walking backward is not 'going out,' and a mark behind the door can't be seen anyway, so the proof for חזקה stands.

steps.title: The כהן cannot open a window to see the mark
steps.stepSummary: אביי blocks a possible comeback: the כהן cannot make a window to see behind the door, because a משנה forbids opening windows to see a mark.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he can open a window in the wall to see it, didn't we learn: In a dark house we don't open windows to see its mark!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is still talking. He shuts down a reply someone might give to his second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the כהן could open a window to see the mark behind the door. אביי answers from a משנה that you may not open windows in a dark house to check for a mark. So the כהן truly cannot see it, and he must rely on חזקה.

phrases.english: And if you say that he opens a window in it –
but didn't we learn: In a dark house

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹתְחִין בּוֹ חַלּוֹנוֹת לִרְאוֹת אֶת נִגְעוֹ!
phrases.english: one may not open windows to see its mark!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens אביי's second answer in Step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that a window could let the כהן see a mark behind the door
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משנה forbids opening windows in a dark house to see a mark.

steps.title: The כהן גדול shows that walking backward counts as going out
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's first answer: the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים walks out backward, and the תורה still calls it 'going out.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You said going out backward is not called going out. The כהן גדול on יום הכפורים proves otherwise. The תורה says he 'goes out,' and we learned that he left the same way he came in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's first answer and brings a case that shows the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses the word 'going out' for the כהן גדול leaving the קודש הקדשים. A משנה teaches that he walked out backward, still facing the ארון. So walking backward does count as 'going out,' and אביי's first answer falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (is an example that shows the point)
The same way he entered (facing inward, so walking backward)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ יְצִיאָה דֶּרֶךְ אֲחוֹרָיו לֹא שְׁמָהּ יְצִיאָה –
phrases.english: That which you said, going out backward is not called going out –
the High Priest on Yom Kippur will prove otherwise,
for "going out" is written about him,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: יָצָא וּבָא לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ כְּנִיסָתוֹ.
phrases.english: and we learned: He went out and came the way he entered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ יְצִיאָה דֶּרֶךְ אֲחוֹרָיו לֹא שְׁמָהּ יְצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's first answer in Step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's claim that walking backward is not 'going out'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תורה calls the כהן גדול's backward exit 'going out.'

steps.title: Windows may be opened once the mark is established
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the window rule: it applies only before a mark is established. Once the mark is known, a window may be opened to see it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you said that in a dark house we don't open windows to see its mark. That is only where the mark was not yet established. Where it was already established, it is established, and a window may be opened.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the other half of אביי's defense, the window rule from Step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on opening windows applies only to a house where no mark has been found yet. Here the כהן already saw a mark, so it is established. He may open a window to keep watching it, and then he does not need חזקה.
steps.whatToRemember: After רבא's two replies, both of אביי's defenses are weakened, and רב אחא בר יעקב's challenge is still standing.

phrases.english: And that which you said: In a dark house

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹתְחִין בּוֹ חַלּוֹנוֹת לִרְאוֹת אֶת נִגְעוֹ –
phrases.english: one may not open windows to see its mark –
this applies only where the mark was not established,
but where it was established – it is established.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ בַּיִת אָפֵל אֵין פּוֹתְחִין בּוֹ חַלּוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's window argument in Step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of the dark-house משנה to support אביי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That משנה applies only before a mark is established, not after.

steps.title: A ברייתא goes against רב אחא בר יעקב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא considers that the כהן might go to his own house to quarantine. This shows that seeing the mark was never required, which goes against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches, not like רב אחא בר יעקב: "And the כהן shall go out from the house." I might think he may go to his own house and quarantine from there? So the פסוק says: "To the doorway of the house."
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבא knocked down אביי's answers, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the proof for חזקה and argues with רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opening line only raises the idea (יכול) that the כהן might quarantine from his own house, and then rejects it with the פסוק. The part that actually works against רב אחא בר יעקב comes at the end of the ברייתא (step 27). There it says a quarantine done from his own house, where he cannot see the mark at all, still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall quarantine (close up the house)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is brought against רב אחא בר יעקב. Its key line comes in Step 27: a quarantine done where the כהן cannot see the mark still counts. Step 28 starts רב אחא בר יעקב's own reading of it.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא דְּלָא כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: It was taught not like Rav Acha bar Yaakov:
"And the priest shall go out from the house" –
I might think he may go into his own house and quarantine?
The verse says: "To the doorway of the house."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא דְּלָא כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the proof after אביי's defenses were weakened
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן does not need to see the mark while he quarantines, so the proof for חזקה stands
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 14:38 that considered quarantining from the כהן's own house

steps.title: The ideal spot: right beside the doorway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the כהן may not stand under the lintel, because that still counts as inside the house. He must be fully outside, standing beside the lintel.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the rule is 'the entrance of the house,' you might think he can stand under the lintel and quarantine. So the פסוק says 'from the house': he must leave the house completely. How does it work? He stands beside the lintel and quarantines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from Step 25. Here the ברייתא sets the ideal place for the כהן to stand: just outside the doorway, next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 already said the כהן should not walk off to his own house, because the פסוק says 'to the entrance of the house.' Now the ברייתא goes the other way: he also cannot stay under the lintel, because 'from the house' means fully out. The answer is the spot in between: beside the lintel, right outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Lintel: the beam above a doorway
'So how is it?': brings together two ideas that seem to pull in different directions

phrases.english: If the rule is "the entrance of the house,"
you might think he may stand under the lintel and quarantine it?
phrases.notes: The lintel is the beam over the doorway. Standing right under it is still treated as being inside.

phrases.english: So the verse says: "from the house"
meaning, not until he leaves the house completely.
So how is it done?
He stands beside the lintel and quarantines the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי פֶּתַח הַבָּיִת יָכוֹל יַעֲמוֹד תַּחַת הַמַּשְׁקוֹף וְיַסְגִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא that Step 25 began, adding the second limit on where the כהן stands.
steps.raayaObject: Against רב אחא בר יעקב: part of the ברייתא that leads up to its ruling that the quarantine counts even without seeing the mark
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא reading ויקרא 14:38 ('from the house… to the entrance of the house')

steps.title: Quarantining from anywhere still works
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the כהן quarantined from his own house or from inside the marked house, the quarantine is still valid, because 'and he shall quarantine the house' means in any case. So seeing the mark is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that if he went into his own house and quarantined, or stood inside the house and quarantined, the quarantine still counts? The פסוק says 'and he shall quarantine the house,' meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the ברייתא. Even after the fact, a quarantine done from far away or from inside the house is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two earlier rules (not from home, not under the lintel) were only the right way to do it from the start. After the fact, the quarantine works anywhere. From his own house the כהן cannot see the mark at all, so this seems to prove that seeing the mark is not required, which goes against רב אחא בר יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: Quarantine: closing up the house for seven days to see if the mark spreads
Quarantined: here, a quarantine that counts
In any case: no matter where he stood

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is contradicting itself. The first rules are how it should be done from the start; this last line is about what still counts after it was already done.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the quarantine works even when the כהן cannot see the mark, then we must be assuming the mark is still there without checking. That is exactly the kind of חזקה the sugya is trying to prove.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם הָלַךְ לְתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ וְהִסְגִּיר,
phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he went into his own house and quarantined,
or if he stood inside the house and quarantined,
phrases.notes: Here 'the house' means the house with the mark, not his own.

phrases.english: that his quarantine is a valid quarantine?
The verse says: "and he shall quarantine the house,"
meaning, in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם הָלַךְ לְתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ וְהִסְגִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and delivers the actual proof that Step 25 pointed toward.
steps.raayaObject: Against רב אחא בר יעקב: the quarantine is valid even when the כהן cannot see the mark
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of 'וְהִסְגִּיר אֶת הַבַּיִת' as 'in any case'

steps.title: Turning to רב אחא בר יעקב's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its defense of רב אחא בר יעקב, about to explain how he reads this ברייתא in line with his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אחא בר יעקב…
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא names רב אחא בר יעקב to prepare the next move: showing how he understands the ברייתא so it does not prove against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is answered yet; the sentence continues in the next part of the daf. The signal is that the ברייתא's proof will not be left standing, and רב אחא בר יעקב will read it his own way.

phrases.english: And Rav Acha bar Yaakov…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the proof in Step 27 by beginning a defense of רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (the ברייתא) to fit his view; details come next
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows the quarantine works even without seeing the mark, against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet given; the גמרא is about to explain his reading.
